headline: This law requires a study of whether the Emancipation National Historic Trail in Texas should be designated a national scenic trail.
what_it_does: The law directs a study of the Emancipation National Historic Trail, a route of about 51 miles from Galveston to Houston, Texas. The route follows the path taken by newly freed slaves and other people of African descent. The study would look at whether the trail should be designated a national scenic trail. The study itself does not make the designation.

who_it_affects.group: National Park Service and the Interior Department
who_it_affects.how: They are responsible for carrying out the study of the trail's possible designation.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of Galveston and Houston, Texas
who_it_affects.how: They live near the trail route, which the study would examine.
Their land may be part of the area reviewed in the study, although the summary does not say how land would be affected.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on January 27, 2020. The official summary does not give a deadline for completing the study.
